detail:
Answering "does twining delete tracked blackboard posts from disk as part of normal operations" — yes, and the largest deletions are unattended, not operator-invoked.

MECHANISM (sqlite backend + export_records, the default):
- blackboard.ts:181-202 — every twining_post recomputes partitionArchivable(before=NO_AGE_CUTOFF, retain=archive.retain_recent). When to_archive.length >= archive.max_blackboard_entries_before_archive (default 500), it fires archiver.archive() fire-and-forget.
- archiver.ts:191 appends the entries to .twining/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-blackboard.jsonl, then archiver.ts:195 calls blackboardStore.dismiss(ids).
- That store is ExportingBlackboardStore (backend-factory.ts:234 withRecordExport). record-export.ts:186-198 dismiss() -> exporter.removePost(entry) -> fs.rmSync on .twining/records/posts/<yyyy-mm>/<ulid>.json.
- .twining/records/ is git-TRACKED. .twining/archive/ is GITIGNORED (.twining/.gitignore line 2). So the archive copy is machine-local and does not ride git.
- Files backend: same outcome via a different shape — blackboard-store.ts:116-158 rewrites tracked .twining/blackboard.jsonl minus the dismissed lines.

EMPIRICAL (this repo): git log --diff-filter=D over .twining/records/posts/ = 1,553 deleted record files in 6 commits. Three of them are ordinary feature/docs commits, each carrying an added post whose summary is literally "Archive: 501 entries archived" / "Archive: 91 entries archived" — the auto-archive signature, i.e. the sweep fired mid-session and the next commit swept up the deletions. Only 3 of 6 were operator-invoked housekeeping/archive_stale.

OTHER DELETION PATHS to tracked post files: twining_dismiss (blackboard-tools.ts:328, full-surface only), twining_archive_stale (housekeeping-tools.ts:233), housekeeping dedup (housekeeping.ts:273), and housekeeping archive:true pass (housekeeping.ts:214). All tombstone into the same gitignored archive/.

SECOND-ORDER: record-ingest.ts:291-296 propagates deletions — a committed post-file deletion DELETEs the corresponding db row on every other clone at next ingest. So one machine's auto-archive erases the post from every collaborator's board on pull.

Exempt from archiving (never deleted this way): decision entries, unresolved need/warning/question entries, and the newest retain_recent (200) archivable entries.

NOT A BUG REPORT — this is documented, deliberate design (LIFE-01..03, D4 retention). The finding worth surfacing is the git-visibility asymmetry: the delete is committable, the preserved copy is not.</detail>
